scope: Wave 1: M2.1 engine governance, M2.2 durability, M2.3 controlled migration

gate_artifacts.command: corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/m2.2
corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/m2.3

claim_limits: This evidence supports CONTROLLED_OPENFILM_READY only, and only after the combined external review passes.
Gate D4.2 is NOT closed: materialization and adoption remain unimplemented.
Gate V1-P0 and V1-Full are NOT claimed.
duration and narration lock integration is NOT_APPLICABLE_APPROVED; no M2.2 typed edit can change either.
render and snapshot_publish have no business runner; only their storage, lease, event and recovery semantics are proven.
AC-005 on the legacy Hypit edit path remains a post-hoc snapshot capture; the migration path is the one that publishes from an isolated stage.
Headed browser automation and human experience are NOT_RUN; no UI automation ran in Wave 1.

The M2.2 per-ticket integrity validator returns non-zero in this capture, and that is expected: it asserts no code changed after M2.2's freeze, and M2.3 deliberately built on it. Its output is recorded verbatim in logs/<sha>/m2.2-integrity.txt rather than tuned to green. This combined capture re-ran M2.2's own gates instead.

cases.title: one writable engine per project; legacy Hypit contract intact
assertions: one binding per project, enforced by a primary key
a migrated copy binds OpenFilm without displacing the source
the legacy D1-D4.2.1 suite still passes

cases.title: every native write entry is translated or refused
assertions: every inventory row registered
no unknown policy
an unregistered operation is denied and recorded

cases.title: a source change outside the Host conflicts and raises attention
assertions: the comparison uses the committed baseline, never a freshly observed digest
the project enters attention and the next write is refused
external bytes are left untouched

cases.title: the pinned upstream is verified byte for byte
assertions: HEAD pinned, checkout clean, and every loaded file hashed
a tampered copy is refused and the original still loads
credential scan reports no findings

cases.title: integer half-open frames at a rational fps, verified as 30/1
assertions: every frame round trips exactly
invalid ranges are refused, never clamped
a short asset is refused rather than looped, frozen or retimed

cases.title: one authoritative transaction machine with predecessor-checked steps
assertions: every transition names its predecessor
legacy journals advance only through the checked helper
no path writes a state without naming where it came from

cases.title: content-addressed snapshots published only when durability is proven
assertions: files then directories bottom-up, then rename, then the parent entry
an unproven step publishes nothing and undoes a rename that already happened

cases.title: three server-computed lock classes; preserve is intent, not authority
assertions: visual always; duration for range changes; narration for subtitle and audio
the client reason text grants nothing
control revision moves with the lock

cases.title: duration and narration lock integration
assertions: no M2.2 typed edit can change duration or narration
the classifier is unit tested with synthetic payloads
an unreachable integration is not recorded as a pass

cases.title: durable jobs with CAS leases, monotonic events and quarantined late results
assertions: a restart keeps jobs and events
a lost lease never becomes a success
two workers cannot both own a job
an unknown cost stays unknown
a late result is quarantined rather than adopted
replay never re-runs a commit

cases.title: the native write gateway is in front of every production write path
assertions: an attention project never reaches the actor
a locked range never reaches the actor
an engine that does not report the capability refuses

cases.title: a deterministic migration plan that blocks what it cannot place
assertions: a valid plan with a stable identity map and a pinned upstream
the same unchanged source always yields the same copy identity
a second key for a migrated source is a conflict, not a duplicate copy

cases.title: the source project reopens and exports after migration, bytes unchanged
assertions: the source digest is identical before and after
the source stays bound to hypit
the copy is exported through the pinned renderer

cases.title: a new project id and one OpenFilm binding, with the source untouched
assertions: the copy has its own project id, revision and binding
the source project's bytes and binding are unchanged

cases.title: three native clips the pinned engine reads and can edit
assertions: the pinned upstream reads the film as three addressable clips
the middle clip is editable through the native mutator
no clip source is a flattened video

cases.title: reopen, export, edit the middle clip, export again
assertions: two real 900-frame MP4s produced by the pinned renderer
the two exports differ; the film is the same length with the same three clips
subtitles and narration travelled with the film

cases.title: an external change in the copy conflicts instead of being accepted
assertions: a changed scene, subtitle or asset produces a conflict
the copy loses writability while the migration keeps its historical state
the changed bytes are left as they are

cases.title: a crash at every boundary converges after a restart
assertions: eight boundaries each leave durable, readable state
no state is written without its predecessor
the source is untouched whatever happened

cases.title: rollback stops writes, restores the source and keeps the copy
assertions: in-flight work is quarantined by id
the source digest equals its pre-migration value
the copy and its report are retained
the source is exported again after rollback

cases.title: the same key replays; a different request conflicts
assertions: replaying a key returns the same migration rather than migrating twice

cases.title: EN/TM/JB and the D1-M1 regression on one frozen commit
assertions: corepack pnpm check green on the combined candidate
no D1-M1 test deleted, skipped or weakened
materialize, adopt, impact and history restore still closed
a fictional operation is still 422
